The '''Kuratowski Prize''' ([[Polish language|Polish]]: ''Nagroda im. Kazimierza Kuratowskiego'') is a Polish annual [[mathematics]] award conferred jointly by the [[Polish Academy of Sciences]] (PAN) and the [[Polish Mathematical Society]] (PTM) for contributions in the field of mathematics granted to individuals under the age of 30.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.impan.pl/en/activities/awards/kazimierz-kuratowski |title=Kazimierz Kuratowski Award |website=impan.pl |access-date=22 November 2024}}</ref> It is named in honour of Polish mathematician and logician [[Kazimierz Kuratowski]] (1896–1980).

==Description and history==
The prize was established in 1981 on the initiative of physician and politician [[Zofia Kuratowska]], who was personally the daughter of Kazimierz Kuratowski. It is presented annually by the [[Institute of Mathematics of the Polish Academy of Sciences]] and the [[Polish Mathematical Society]] (''Polskie Towarzystwo Matematyczne''). The Kuratowski Prize ceremony takes place during the scientific session of the Polish Mathematical Society and the laureate of the prize is invited to give a speech on a chosen subject. It is considered the most prestigious award for young mathematicians in Poland.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://naukawpolsce.pl/aktualnosci/news%2C400715%2Cnagroda-im-k-kuratowskiego-dla-matematyka-z-pwr.html |language=pl |title=Nagroda im. K. Kuratowskiego dla matematyka z PWr |website=naukawpolsce.pl |date=9 June 2014 |access-date=22 November 2024}}</ref>

In 2015, [[Joanna Kułaga-Przymus]] became the first woman to be awarded the prize.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.ptm.org.pl/zawartosc/joanna-ku%C5%82aga-przymus-i-mateusz-micha%C5%82ek-laureatami-nagrody-im-kazimierza-kuratowskiego-20 |language=pl |title=Joanna Kaługa-Przymus i Mateusz Michałek laureatami Nagrody im. Kazimierza Kuratowskiego 2015 |website=ptm.org.pl |date=20 May 2015 |access-date=22 November 2024}}</ref> As of 2026, there have been two women mathematicians to receive this recognition, the other being [[Agnieszka Hejna]] (2023).

Notable laureates of the prize have included two [[Prize of the Foundation for Polish Science]] winners: [[Mariusz Lemańczyk]] (1987) and [[Tomasz Łuczak]] (1997); [[Erdős Prize]] winner [[Wojciech Samotij]] (2013); and [[Polish Mathematical Society#Stefan Banach Prize|Stefan Banach Prize]] winner [[Jerzy Weyman]] (1984).
